title: The frontend lets a user delete a notification and cancel an amendment from the dashboard; DR1 has neither journey, and whether they are in scope for DR1 parity is unsettled.

finding.frontend: Every card on the dashboard offers a Delete link, and a card being amended also offers Cancel amendment (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js:18-67). Delete leads to a confirmation page headed "Delete this notification?" saying "This cannot be undone." with a red "Yes, delete notification" and "No, return to dashboard". Cancel amendment leads to "Cancel this amendment?" saying the changes since amending started will be discarded and the submitted version restored. Submitted cards also offer Amend, which is where the amendment being cancelled comes from.
finding.prototype: A DR1 user has neither. The card offers Copy as new and View and nothing else (app/views/dashboard.html:257-262), and the two journeys the frontend has are unreachable: the delete page redirects to the dashboard unless the session carries the design-release-2 flag (app/routes.js:5607-5613), and cancel-amend does the same (app/routes.js:9652-9655). There is no DR1 page to compare either frontend page against, which is why the corpus pairs neither of them.
finding.difference: This is the one question in this slice that needs a person rather than more evidence. Two readings are both consistent with what is on the page. Either delete and amend are design-release-2 features that shipped early in the frontend, in which case they are out of scope here and this comparison should record no finding about the pages themselves; or they are capabilities DR1 assumed without drawing, in which case DR1 is silent rather than opposed and the frontend pages need reviewing against DR2 designs, not this one. What settles it is a statement from the designer on whether delete and amend were in the DR1 scope: if they were, DR1's dashboard card is missing a Delete action and the absence is a prototype gap; if they were not, both frontend journeys are ahead of the signed-off design and belong to the next comparison. Until then, treat the two frontend pages as unassessed rather than as defects, and raise nothing about their copy, their button pattern or their confirmation wording.
finding.falsifiedBy: Reaching a delete or a cancel-amendment page in the prototype at its root mount, without a design-release-2 session.
finding.correction: Correct as written, correctly kept as one finding covering both journeys, and the session-guard mechanism is right. Verified: isDesignRelease2SessionData is true only when the session carries the design-release-2 or design-release-2.1 flag (app/routes.js:6207-6212), and a root-mount session carries neither, so both guards fire and both pages redirect away. The cancel-amend guard at app/routes.js:9652-9655 is exactly as cited. The delete guard is slightly understated: it is a two-part test, redirecting unless the session carries the flag AND the request carries a submitted or reference query parameter, so the flag alone would not be enough. The frontend side is exact — rowActions attaches the delete action to all three status branches and cancel amendment only to the amending branch — and both confirmation pages read word for word as described in evidence/frontend@76a864ba/page/fe-delete-notification.png and fe-cancel-amend.png. Two things worth saying about the band. First, the finding contract already rules amend and delete out: it lists them among the things that are an onlyFrontend observation rather than a defect, to be said once in the slice covering those screens, which is precisely what this file does. Second, no frontend work follows under either of the two readings offered — if the journeys are design-release-2 features they belong to the next comparison, and if DR1 assumed them without drawing them the gap is in the prototype, not the frontend. So disputed is the right band and the designer's answer changes what this belongs to, not what anyone builds. ONE CONTROL CANNOT BE CROPPED, AND IS KEPT NAMED. 'Cancel amendment' is the link on a dashboard card, and it only appears on a card whose notification is being amended. The captured dashboard holds one draft card, offering Delete and Copy as new and nothing else, so the string occurs in no frontend capture — the only place 'Cancel' appears is on fe-cancel-amend itself, as the breadcrumb, the page title and the heading 'Cancel this amendment?'. The state that would show the link is a dashboard captured with a notification in the amending status; it was not captured because the corpus's dashboard states are the empty one and the one-draft one. The control stays named so the report keeps reporting the gap rather than closing it quietly. The heading 'Cancel this amendment?' has been added alongside it, because the confirmation page the link leads to is captured and is the half of the journey this corpus can actually show; the Delete control already crops on fe-delete-notification.
